segments.narration: A tank of nuclear waste exploded and nobody was told. The southern Urals, September 1957.
Mayak made plutonium for Soviet bombs. One waste tank lost its cooling, baked itself dry, and went off with the force of seventy tonnes of TNT.
The blast threw a radioactive plume hundreds of kilometres downwind. Villagers kept working their fields for a week before anyone came to move them. How do you hide something that size?
You leave the town off the map. Chelyabinsk-40 was printed nowhere, so the accident got named after Kyshtym, the nearest place that officially existed.
Twenty million curies. Ten thousand people moved. No admission until 1989. It is still the only accident anywhere rated level six.

verdicts.claim: On 29 September 1957 a tank of liquid high-level nuclear waste exploded at the Mayak plant in the southern Urals, and the Soviet Union concealed the accident.
verdicts.note: 93% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 2 number(s)

verdicts.claim: Mayak was a plutonium reprocessing plant for Soviet nuclear weapons; a cooling system failure let the waste dry to ammonium nitrate and acetate residue, which exploded with a force of at least 70 tons of TNT.
verdicts.note: 83% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 1 number(s)

verdicts.claim: About 2 million curies went into a plume spread over hundreds of kilometres, and evacuations only began on 6 October 1957, a week after the explosion.
verdicts.note: 82% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 3 number(s)

verdicts.claim: The plant stood in the closed city of Chelyabinsk-40, which was not marked on maps, so the accident was named after Kyshtym, the nearest town that was.
verdicts.note: 94% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 1 number(s)

verdicts.claim: An estimated 20 million curies was released in total, about 10,000 people were evacuated, the Soviet government only began declassifying the documents in 1989, and it remains the only accident rated INES level 6.
verdicts.note: 79% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 4 number(s)
